To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
capital inflows have a positive impact on economic growth in recipient countries.

(1) capital flows to emerging markets are mainly driven by push factors in the donor economy; (2) the pull factors of the recipient economy play a more significant role in attracting capital flows to advanced economies; (3) capital flows to advanced countries are more stable than to emerging markets; and (4) capital inflows are beneficial for economic growth in both types of countries.

(a) the capital flows are driven by both push factors (such as domestic financial development) and pull factors (such as economic growth, inflation, and exchange rate), (b) the push and pull factors are equally important in explaining capital inflows to the recipient economies, and (c) the push factors are more important for the emerging market countries than advanced economies.
